# uia

uia is a design system for AI products. It already encodes the taste: calm
greys, one ink for actions, one colour for "this needs you", mono micro-labels,
white pages with hairline cards and quiet motion. Your job is not to invent a style but
to compose the existing pieces so the result looks like the designer built it.

## How to work

1. **Find what exists.** Read `src/components/{ui,ds,parts,chat}` in the
   project. If a piece you need is missing, install it from the registry
   before writing anything (`npx shadcn@latest add franklinjavier/uia/<item>`,
   items listed in `references/components.md`). Writing a lookalike by hand is
   how systems drift. Check the setup once: the main CSS imports
   `./typeset.css` after Tailwind, the app is wrapped in `TooltipProvider`,
   and `AGENTS.md` has a "UI: uia design system" section pointing at
   `.agents/skills/uia/SKILL.md` (with `CLAUDE.md` importing `@AGENTS.md`)
   so the next agent finds this skill; add whichever is missing, appending,
   never replacing.
2. **Start from the closest example.** uia ships complete widgets built by
   the designer (`references/examples.md`; install with
   `npx shadcn@latest add franklinjavier/uia/examples`). Open the one closest
   to the request, render it, and copy its structure — anatomy, panel split,
   spacing, the pieces that carry the data — then change the content. The
   moves behind them are in `references/grammar.md`. Rules alone don't make
   screens look related; imitating the examples does.
3. **Pick the pattern before the pixels.** Is this a widget, a chat, or a
   moment inside a chat? For anything where the agent needs the person, read
   `references/hitl.md` first; the pattern decides the components.
4. **Compose parts, don't restyle them.** Every component is a set of parts
   (`Widget` → `WidgetHeader`/`WidgetPanel`/`WidgetFooter`, `ActionCard` →
   `ActionCardHeader`/`…Status`/`…Panel`/`…Actions`). Arrange parts and pass
   `className` for layout only (gap, width, padding). If you are overriding
   colours, radii or font sizes, stop: use a token or a variant instead
   (`references/tokens.md`).
5. **Use the tokens by meaning.** `brand` = the primary action (ink).
   `attention` = something waits on the person. Semantic tones only for state.
   Never use a colour because it looks nice.
6. **Verify in the browser**, light and dark, by walking the real flow (see
   the checklist below). Most of what makes uia feel right — spacing, motion,
   states — is only visible when it runs.

## The look, in rules (and why)

- **Hierarchy by size and colour, not weight.** Titles are 15–16px regular;
  numbers are large and light. Bold is rare. Heavy weights make the calm
  surfaces look shouty.
- **Mono uppercase `eyebrow` is the second voice**: labels, units, meta lines,
  provider names, counters (`<span className="eyebrow text-muted-foreground">`).
  It carries metadata so body text can stay plain.
- **No frames by default.** The page is plain `background` (white); a
  `Widget` is just header + white panels + footer, aligned on one edge. Use
  `<Widget variant="framed">` (grey `surface` shell + shadow) only when the
  widget must read as an object among neighbours (dashboards, floating
  panels). Never add a grey page or decorative backdrop. Inside a message, cards use a faint `bg-muted/30` with no shadow (ActionCard) or
  `bg-card` with a hairline `border`. Prefer hairline borders over filled
  blocks; solid grey fills read as heavy (the user asked for minimalism).
- **One indicator per meaning.** The `AgentOrb` is the only thing that moves
  while the agent works; trace lines shimmer, they don't spin. Don't add icons
  that repeat what a word already says.
- **Buttons speak one language**: primary `default` (ink), secondary
  `secondary` (grey fill), tertiary `ghost`; in cards use `size="sm"`, pill
  shaped, left-aligned. The `brand` variant is for a widget's main CTA.
- **Numbers**: `tabular-nums` only on numeric cells/values — never on a whole
  row or table (in Inter it widens hyphens: "Re - issue").
- **Motion** comes from `@/lib/motion` (`springSnappy`, `springSoft`,
  `easeOut`, `enter`). Things appear where they land (fade + ≤4px lift). No
  layout animations inside a streaming transcript: content moves under them
  and they fly in from the top. When a part changes state, wrap it in
  `PartTransition`.
- **Moves show where things went.** In a list that isn't a streaming
  transcript (an inbox, a queue, a board), acting on an item never makes it
  blink away: it leaves toward where it goes (an answered card sinks toward
  "Answered today": `exit={{ opacity: 0, y: 20, scale: 0.98 }}`), the items
  around it glide into the gap (`layout="position"` with `springSoft`,
  inside `AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"` + `LayoutGroup`, sections
  too), and it arrives from the direction it came (`y: -12` from above),
  glowing once (`bg-muted` fading over ~1 s) so the eye finds it. Newest
  first, so the trip is short. Undo plays it backwards.
- **Chat turns animate themselves.** `ChatTurn` plays the entrance: what
  the person sends lands with a fade, a 8px lift and a blur clearing; the
  answer follows 120 ms later; a thread's history (opened, reloaded) just
  appears. Don't add your own wrapper animations around turns.
- **Navigation icons nudge on hover**: one small gesture per icon that says
  what the place is (inbox drops, layers lift, history rewinds, scale
  weighs), played once per hover, never looping — motion variants on the
  button, see `NUDGE` in `example-davinci`. A conversation entry uses the
  still `AgentOrb` (no chat-bubble icon) and wakes it on hover. Don't size
  nav icons with `[&_svg]:size-4` on the button: it shrinks the orb too.
- **Verbs for actions, switches for policies.** Something done once
  (approve, revert, deploy) is a button whose label is the verb. Something
  that stays on until changed (a rule, an automation, a fallback) is a
  `Switch`, with the whole row as its label; the off state says its effect
  in the meta line ("Off · these come back to your inbox"). No confirmation
  for a switch: it's undoable by flipping it back.
- **Separators are straight hairlines.** A `border-t` on a rounded row
  curls up at both ends; draw the line inside the padding instead
  (`WidgetListRow` does). Never put a border on one side of a rounded box.
- **A widget is a component with props; demo data lives outside.** Build
  data views as pure components (`components/widgets/*`: data in via props,
  UI state inside, actions out via callbacks, pending states as props) and
  keep fixtures and simulations in the example. The same component renders
  on a page and, at `Widget size="sm"`, inside a chat reply — one shell,
  two densities, never a chat-only copy.
- **shadcn first.** Before building a piece, check the shadcn catalog
  (`bunx shadcn add <name>`): Badge, Alert, Sheet, Attachment, Marker,
  HoverCard, Table, Tabs, Field… uia's pieces are built on them
  (`StatusBadge` = Badge, `ChatError` = Alert, `AttachmentChip` =
  Attachment, `TranscriptEvent` = Marker). Keep uia's look and motion with
  `className` on top of the shadcn API; customise the copied file only when
  that can't work.
- **Every screen has an address.** In an app, each view and sub-view is a
  route (`/app/rules`, `/app/threads/blog`): reload keeps the place, back
  and forward work, a link can point at it. Views take `view` +
  `onViewChange` from the router rather than holding it in state; the logo
  or orb goes home. Simulations and modes ride in the query (`?busy`).
- **An app carries its own theme toggle** (sun/moon ghost icon button at
  the foot of the side nav, in the header on phones), using `useTheme`
  from `theme-provider`. Don't rely on the host page to offer it.
- **Design for load.** Before calling a list done, run it with ten times
  the data (dozens of tasks, not three). What needs the person sorts
  first, the list folds after a handful ("Show 20 more" in the footer), and
  an aggregate carries the shape (counts per stage under the stage names,
  "22 in flight · 4 queued" in the header). Keep that simulation behind a
  dashed "Simulation" switch or a URL flag, never in the default state.
- **Errors point at what is missing**, in one quiet line, without painting
  fields red.
- **Every control does something.** No info icons, settings sliders, close
  buttons, ⋮ menus or status footers that are only there to look complete.
  If it has no action or no information the person needs, leave it out;
  empty space is fine.
- **Build what was asked.** A widget request gets a widget: no page header,
  breadcrumb, tagline or hero copy around it. A page request gets a page
  (`references/grammar.md` §8).
- **No instructions on screen.** "Select a suite to filter", "Hover a GPU",
  "Click a node to focus" are signs the affordance is weak; make it
  discoverable instead (hover state, cursor, the visual reacting).
- **Don't label the data as fake.** No "demo", "sample data", "no API
  connected" pills or footers; mock data should look like real data.
- **Colour only what needs a look.** In a list of deltas, regressions get a
  tone; improvements stay muted. A column of green badges is noise.
- **Adapting a reference or mockup:** keep its structure and behaviour, not
  its decoration. Its accent colour becomes `brand` (ink); its "needs you"
  moments become `attention`; repeated indicators (a dot *and* a badge for
  the same state) collapse into one.
- **Say each fact once.** If the meter already reads "86% used", the label,
  the meta line and the alert don't repeat it; each says something new
  (what's left, when it resets, what to do). Repetition is noise that
  competes with the one line that matters.
- **Tone escalates with severity.** `neutral` → `warning` (getting close) →
  `destructive` (over, failed, blocked). Each step changes the colour *and*
  the words; two states with the same tone read as the same state.
- **Speak the user's language and locale.** Copy, currency, dates and number
  formats follow the product's audience (e.g. pt-BR → "R$ 1.287,05",
  "20 de out."), not the model's defaults. If it isn't clear, follow the
  language the request was written in.

## Generative UI inside a chat

A reply is prose plus *parts*. Text, reasoning and sources render themselves
(`ChatTurn`/`ChatParts`). Every tool you add gets one entry in a typed
registry — that is where your UI goes:

```tsx
const tools = defineTools<MyMessage>()({
  searchDocs: { phase: "searching", render: (part) => <Trace><ToolLine … /></Trace> },
  askQuestions: { client: true, render: (part, ctx) => <AskUser … onSubmit={(a) => ctx.addOutput({ answers: a })} /> },
  deleteFiles: { render: (part, ctx) => <Confirmation … onAllow={() => ctx.respond(true)} onDeny={() => ctx.respond(false)} /> },
})
```

`client: true` marks tools the person completes (questions, drafts): the chat
waits on them and continues when `ctx.addOutput` is called. Approval tools use
the AI SDK `needsApproval` flow and `ctx.respond`. State that isn't a tool
call (a plan's progress) is a data part rendered through `defineData`;
same `id` = updated in place. Full wiring: `references/chat.md`.

Don't reinvent the common moments; each has a part and a place
(`chat.md` → "The moments every chat needs"): toggles that light while the
agent uses them, attachments with a hover gist, a chart in the reply, a
`Plan` that ticks off, `ConnectPrompt` docked above the composer,
`ChatError` with a retry that can switch model, Regenerate, and `ChatPill`
when minimised.

When nothing prebuilt fits, the agent **composes a surface**: A2UI v0.9
messages against the uia catalog (layout, data, display, input and whole
blocks), rendered by `<Surface>` on a page or `size="sm"` in a reply. The
agent sends names, enums and data, never styling or code. Read
`references/surfaces.md` before building agent-composed screens.

## Human-in-the-loop in one paragraph

Ask before guessing (`AskUser`: one question at a time, A/B/C keys, free
answer, × to skip). A consequential draft *is* the approval (`DraftCard`:
fields + editable body + "Send email"/"Discard"). Side effects wait at a gate
(`Confirmation`: "Assistant wants to …" + "Approval needed" + Allow/Deny).
Once settled, every moment shrinks to a record that can reopen (`ResolvedRow`,
or the answered-question card for a single question); declined ones dim. Never
claim something happened that didn't. Details and copy rules:
`references/hitl.md`.

## Before you say it's done

**Review it like the designer would.** Screenshot your screen and the
closest example side by side, light and dark, and ask: does it look like
the same person made both? Check the hero (one number, its limit visible,
a meta line), the list (titled, eyebrow headers, linked to the visual),
the footer (live meta, one action), the spacing, and that nothing on screen
is decoration. Fix what differs before reporting.

- [ ] Started from the closest example and kept its structure.
- [ ] Every piece came from the project or the registry; no hand-made lookalikes.
- [ ] No hard-coded colours, radii or font sizes; tokens and variants only.
- [ ] Ran it: light **and** dark, at the real container size, and on a phone
      (375 px emulated; nothing sticks out, nothing is crushed — grammar §9).
- [ ] Walked every state: empty, streaming, waiting on the person, each answer
      (approve, deny, discard, skip), resolved, error.
- [ ] Typecheck the app for real: in the Vite template `tsc --noEmit` on the
      root config checks nothing (`files: []`); run
      `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`.
- [ ] Reloaded on every view: you stay where you were; back/forward work.
- [ ] Ran it with 10× the data: nothing truncates into nonsense, what needs
      the person is on top, long lists fold.
- [ ] Every switch, toggle and icon has its hover/focus state; the theme
      toggle is reachable from the app itself.
- [ ] Console clean after a fresh reload.
- [ ] Re-read `references/pitfalls.md` for anything you touched.

- `references/grammar.md` — the moves the examples are made of: anatomy, hero, lists as legends, data viz, copy, spacing, pages, mobile, agent apps (inbox, threads, rules).
- `references/tokens.md` — every token, what it means, when to use it.

# Tokens

All tokens live in the project's main CSS (installed by `franklinjavier/uia/theme`)
and are exposed as Tailwind utilities (`bg-surface`, `text-attention`, …).
Use them by **meaning**. If no token means what you need, the design probably
doesn't need it.

## Surfaces (back to front)

| Token | Utility | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--surface` | `bg-surface` | The shell of a `Widget variant="framed"`. The only grey layer; most widgets don't use it. |
| `--background` / `--card` | `bg-background`, `bg-card` | The page (body default) and card level: panels, the composer, resolved rows. Plain white in light. Don't add a grey page behind widgets. |
| `--muted` | `bg-muted`, `bg-muted/60` | Inset or pending: ActionCard body (`/30`), hover, code blocks (`bg-muted/25`). Use translucent steps rather than new greys. |
| `--popover` | `bg-popover` | Menus and select popups. |

Shadow: `shadow-widget` only on a framed widget's shell; `shadow-xs` on cards; nothing
heavier inside a transcript.

Borders are hairlines: `border-border` (or `/70`, `/80`). In dark mode the border
is 9% white, so the same class works in both themes.

## Text

| Utility | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `text-foreground` | Body, titles, values. |
| `text-muted-foreground` | Descriptions, secondary labels, eyebrow labels. |
| `text-faint-foreground` | Tertiary meta: provider names in a list, counters, timestamps next to stronger meta. |

## Colour with meaning

| Token | Meaning | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` (ink: near-black in light, near-white in dark) | The primary action / the product's voice | `Button` default and `brand` variant, `ComposerSubmit`, `TickMeter`, Segmented indicator |
| `attention` (orange) | **Something waits on the person** — and nothing else | "Approval needed" pill, `ChatStatus` waiting, `StatusDot tone="attention"` |
| `success` | Finished well | done pills, ready dot |
| `warning` | Degraded, needs a look later | quota near limit |
| `info` | Neutral information with a hue | rarely; prefer muted text |
| `destructive` | Failed or irreversible | error pill, delete confirmations |

Rules of thumb:

- One orange thing on screen at a time, ideally. If two parts both need the
  person, they are probably one decision.
- Never use `attention` to decorate (badges, highlights, links). It loses its
  meaning the moment it's decorative.
- Tones escalate: `neutral` (fine) → `warning` (close to a limit, degraded)
  → `destructive` (over the limit, failed). Don't stop at `warning` when the
  limit is actually hit.
- State tones come with words. A dot alone is not enough: `StatusBadge` pairs
  dot + label; `ActionCardStatus` is a pill with text.
- Charts use `--chart-1…5` (from the shadcn theme), not semantic tones.

## Type

- **Inter** for everything; `font-mono` (**Geist Mono**) for code, kbd and
  the `eyebrow`.
- `eyebrow` utility = mono, 11px, uppercase, wide tracking. The second voice
  for labels and metadata. Pair it with `text-muted-foreground` or
  `text-faint-foreground`.
- Sizes in use: 11 (eyebrow), 12 (`text-xs` meta), 14 (`text-sm` body,
  chat), 15 (card titles, question titles), 16 (`text-base` widget titles),
  36 (`text-4xl` stat values, `tracking-[-0.03em]`).
- Weights: regular almost everywhere; `font-medium` for a label that anchors
  a row (ResolvedRow label, ActionCard title). Avoid `font-semibold`/`bold`.
- Long-form assistant prose goes through `Markdown` (typeset preset
  `.typeset-chat`); don't style prose by hand.

## Radius

From `--radius` (0.625rem): cards `rounded-2xl`, widget shell `rounded-3xl`,
buttons and composer controls `rounded-full` (pills), small icon tiles
`rounded-md`. Nested radii shrink inwards (shell 3xl → panel 2xl → row xl).

## Motion

`@/lib/motion`:

| Preset | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `enter` (0.28s ease-out-quint) | Something appears: fade + `y: 4`. |
| `easeOut` (0.2s) | Small UI responses: hover reveals, icon swaps. |
| `springSnappy` | Indicators that follow a choice (Segmented thumb). |
| `springSoft` | Height changes (`PartTransition`, disclosures). |

Respect the existing animations; don't add bounce, slide-from-edge, or
staggered list entrances inside a transcript.

# Components What to reach for, by job. Paths are the default shadcn aliases (`@/components/…`). Install anything missing with: ```bash npx shadcn@latest add franklinjavier/uia/ # one piece (deps come along) npx shadcn@latest add franklinjavier/uia/chat franklinjavier/uia/hitl # bundles ``` Use `--overwrite` if the project already has stock `button`, `select`, … — uia ships tuned versions. Then make sure `typeset.css` is imported after Tailwind and the app is wrapped in `TooltipProvider`. Every component accepts `className` and passes props through; every part has a `data-slot` you can target from a parent (`*:data-[slot=…]:…`) instead of forking the component. ## Contents 1. System pieces (`ds/`) 2. Generative-UI parts (`parts/`) 3. Chat kit (`chat/`) 4. Primitives (`ui/`) 5. Bundles and item names 6. Widgets (`widgets/`) and the app shell (`app/`) --- ## 1. System pieces — `@/components/ds/*` ### Widget (`widget`) A self-contained tool surface: header → panels → footer. ```tsx Knowledge base …main content… …a second, separate block… Synced 2m ago ``` - `Widget variant="plain"` (default): no shell; children gap 2; header and footer align with the panels' edge. Right inside chats and white pages. - `Widget variant="framed"`: the floating shell (`rounded-3xl bg-surface p-1 shadow-widget`, gap 1). For dashboards with neighbours, floating panels. - `Widget size="sm"`: message density (header/footer `min-h-8`, title 14px medium, panels `p-3.5`, the `lg` stat steps down to 24px). The same widget inside a chat reply, a side panel or a dense grid. `ChartCard` and `Findings` are compositions of it; never build a second shell. - `WidgetPanel`: `rounded-2xl bg-card p-5` hairline ring. Use several panels rather than dividers inside one. - `WidgetHeader`/`WidgetFooter`: no card of their own; padding follows the variant (don't override it). - `WidgetDescription` for one muted line under the title; `WidgetMeta` is eyebrow-styled. - `WidgetSectionTitle`: a small heading inside a panel ("Routes", "Agents"). - `WidgetList` > `WidgetListHeader` + `WidgetListRow`: rows inside a panel, hairline between rows. Put the same `grid-cols-[…]` on the header and every row; header cells are `eyebrow text-muted-foreground`. A row with `onClick` becomes a button (`selected` → `bg-muted`); `dimmed` fades it. - **One interaction for a list linked to a visual** (chart, graph, illustration): hovering a row previews it (other rows `dimmed`, the visual follows), clicking selects it. Don't invent another model per widget. ```tsx setHovered(null)}> Agents Status {agents.map((a) => ( setHovered(a.id)} onClick={() => setSelected(a.id)}>… ))} ``` ### Stat (`stat`) `Stat` > `StatLabel` (eyebrow) · `StatValue size="lg|sm"` (light, tabular) · `StatUnit` · `StatMeta` (mono, faint). Big numbers, never bold. ### Segmented (`segmented`) Base UI toggle group with a moving thumb. `variant="mono"` (eyebrow labels, for ranges like 1D/1W/1M) or `"sans"` (view switches). ```tsx 7D 30D ``` ### Status (`status`) `StatusDot tone` and `StatusBadge tone` with tones `neutral | success | warning | info | destructive | brand | attention`. Pulse only for live states. ### MeterBar (`meter-bar`) A value against its limit, with the limit visible. One segment for a plain meter, several for a breakdown; `markers` label thresholds; `highlighted` fades the other segments (link it to the list's hover). `min` zooms into a narrow range (pass rates 60–100%) so close markers don't collide. ```tsx ({ id: m.id, value: m.cost, color: m.color }))} markers={[{ value: 1200, label: "80%" }, { value: 1500, label: "Budget" }]} highlighted={hovered} /> ``` ### BarSeries (`bar-series`) `` — one hue (`chart-1`), bars at 30%, the one that matters (`highlight`, default the latest) at full strength with its value above. Hover/focus a bar to read it; the label row keeps only the first, last and hovered labels. ### Sparkline (`sparkline`) `` — line over a soft area, dashed mean, last point marked. Pair with a big number and an eyebrow for the window ("Last 64 s"). ### StageTrack (`stage-track`) Where something is in a fixed sequence, on one line: dots joined by hairlines, each `done | active | waiting | failed | todo`. Dots without names are a puzzle: every track must have its stage names in view. In a list, put them once in a header with `` (same grid as the tracks; when rows stack on narrow widths and the track spans the row, give the stacked layout its own labels row too). A track that stands alone (a detail panel) uses ``. Over many tracks (dozens of tasks), give each label a `count` (how many sit at that stage), sort what needs the person first, and fold the list after a handful: the counts show where work piles up without reading every row. Pass `statusLabels` in the product's language for screen readers. ### TickMeter (`tick-meter`) Progress as hairline ticks: ``. Colour = `currentColor`. ### NumberTicker (`number-ticker`) Animated number: ` v.toFixed(1)} />`. ### AgentOrb (`agent-orb`) The agent's presence. `phase`: `idle | connecting | thinking | searching | working | composing | waiting`; `size` 20/32/64; `active` (false = paused, dimmed). It is **the** working indicator — one per live turn, plus optionally one in the header/empty state. Don't add spinners next to it. ### ModelIcon (`model-icons`) ``, monochrome, `currentColor`. For model pickers and attributions. --- ## 2. Generative-UI parts — `@/components/parts/*` Read `hitl.md` for when to use which. Summary: | Component | Item | Job | | --- | --- | --- | | `ActionCard` + parts | `action-card` | The shape of every HITL moment. Compose your own cards from it. | | `ResolvedRow` | `action-card` | A settled moment: one line, expandable record, `muted` when it didn't go ahead. | | `TranscriptEvent` | `action-card` | Small centred line for in-progress or system events ("Creating 4 issues…"); shadcn `Marker` with a fade-in. # Human-in-the-loop

A generative UI earns trust by being clear about three things: what the agent
needs from the person, what will happen if they say yes, and what actually
happened afterwards. Every pattern below exists to answer one of those.

## Choosing the pattern

| The agent… | Pattern | Component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is missing information it can't infer | Ask | `AskUser` (client tool) |
| produced something that will go out in the person's name (email, post, message, PR description) | Draft = approval | `DraftCard` (client tool) |
| wants to run something with side effects (create, delete, pay, invite, deploy) | Gate | `Confirmation` (AI SDK `needsApproval`) |
| changed something visual that ships to users | Preview acceptance | `PreviewApproval` (before/after, accept or ask for changes) |
| needs a choice between a few concrete options with consequences | Custom ActionCard | `ActionCard` parts + buttons per option |
| is doing something the person should see but not stop | Trace | `ToolLine` / `TranscriptEvent` |

If you're unsure whether to gate: does it change something outside the chat,
cost money, or reach other people? Gate it. Reading and searching never gate.

## The life of a moment

Every HITL part has the same three phases. Design all three, always.

1. **Asking** — a full card (`ActionCard` family). Title says *who wants to do
   what* ("Assistant wants to create 4 issues in Linear"), a status pill in
   `attention` says it's waiting ("Approval needed", "Needs your answer"),
   then the minimum context, details behind a disclosure, a trust note, and
   the actions. The chat's `waiting` is true; the composer should say
   "Answer above to continue…".
2. **Working** (if the result isn't instant) — `TranscriptEvent` with a
   `shimmer` line ("Creating 4 issues…"). Not a spinner; the orb already
   moves.
3. **Resolved** — the card shrinks to a record:
   - `ResolvedRow` with icon · label · past-tense summary, expandable to the
     record (the list created, the body sent, the answers given).
   - `muted` (dimmed) when it didn't go ahead: denied, discarded, skipped. Use
     an icon that says so (`BanIcon`, `Trash2Icon`).
   - A single answered question becomes a small static card (question +
     `AnswerKey`) instead of a row — the answer is the content.

Wrap the part in `PartTransition state={…}` keyed on the phase so the card
closes into its record (height eases, content crossfades) instead of jumping.

## Copy

- Title: "Assistant wants to {verb} {object} {where}". Concrete numbers and
  names ("12 threads", "#launch", "Linear"), not "some items".
- Status pill: short state, not an instruction. "Approval needed", "Ready",
  "Sent", "Denied".
- Description: one or two lines of *why* or *what exactly*. Skip if the title
  says it all.
- Disclosure labels: "Show the {thing}" / "Hide the {thing}".
- Note (fine print): what the person can undo or where to find it later. "You
  can close or edit them in Linear afterwards." "Nothing is sent until you
  press Send."
- Buttons: the verb of the action ("Send email", "Create issues", "Archive"),
  not "OK"/"Confirm". Decline is "Deny", "Discard" or "Not now" depending on
  what's being declined.
- Resolved summary: past tense, with the outcome. "Sent email · Beta list ·
  1,284 people", "Denied · create 4 issues".

## Honesty rules

- **Never claim an action happened** that the tool output didn't confirm. The
  assistant's follow-up text reads from the output ("Sent to 1,284 people")
  and handles denial plainly ("Okay, I didn't create them.").
- **Respect the answer.** If the person picked "Formal", the draft is formal;
  if they skipped, say what you assumed.
- **Edits are the person's.** A `DraftCard` body is editable; send the edited
  body (`onSend(body)`), and show that body in the resolved record.
- One decision per card. Don't stack two gates; merge them or sequence them.

## Questions (`AskUser`)

```tsx
<AskUser
  questions={[{ id: "channel", question: "Which channel is this for?", choices: ["Email", "Blog", "X thread"] }]}
  onSubmit={(answers) => ctx.addOutput({ answers })}
  onSkip={() => ctx.addOutput({ answers: {} })}
/>
```

- 1–3 questions, each with 2–4 choices; a free-text answer is always
  available. One question at a time (Back/Next for several).
- Ask only what changes the result. If a sensible default exists, use it and
  say so instead of asking.
- Answered: `<AskUserAnswered questions answers />` (single → card, multiple
  → expandable row, skipped → muted row).

## Drafts (`DraftCard`)

```tsx
const draft: Draft = {
  kind: "New email", app: "Mail", icon: "mail",
  title: "The new dashboard is live",
  fields: [{ label: "To", value: "Beta list" }, { label: "From", value: "product@example.com" }],
  summary: "Beta list · 1,284 people",
  body: "Hi there,\n\n…",
  sendLabel: "Send email", sentVerb: "Sent email",
}
<DraftCard draft={draft} state={status} sentBody={sentBody}
  onSend={(body) => ctx.addOutput({ status: "sent", body })}
  onDiscard={() => ctx.addOutput({ status: "discarded" })} />
```

The card is its own approval: no separate Confirmation after it.

## Approvals (`Confirmation`)

Server tool declared with `needsApproval: true` in the AI SDK. The part comes
in as `state: "approval-requested"`; answer with `ctx.respond(true|false)`.
Use `toolPhase(part)` to get `running | done | error | denied` afterwards.
Full example: the `createIssues` entry in `chat.md`.

## Building a new HITL card

When none of the ready-made ones fit (choose a meeting slot, pick a plan,
approve a refund amount), compose `ActionCard` parts. Keep the order:
header (title + status) → description → panel(s) → note → actions. Put the
choice inside a panel (a list of `Item`s, `ActionCardFields`, a small form),
keep one primary button, and give it a resolved state the same way. Make it a
`client: true` tool if the person's choice *is* the tool output.

## Decisions outside the conversation

On a page next to the conversation (dashboards, workspaces), surface every
open decision as a `DecisionChip` in a "needs you" strip at the top. The
chip never decides: it scrolls to the full card in the conversation and
highlights it briefly. One place to answer, one place to look.

# Chat

How to assemble a chat with the uia kit. Built on the AI SDK v5+ (`ai`,
`@ai-sdk/react`); the kit adds state, the tool registry and the pieces.

## 1. Type the message and its tools

Tools are typed once on the server (or with `createChat` for client-only
demos) and the UI derives from `UIMessage<…, …, Tools>`:

```ts
import type { InferUITools, UIMessage } from "ai"
export type ChatMessage = UIMessage<unknown, never, InferUITools<typeof serverTools>>
```

Server tools that need consent: `tool({ …, needsApproval: true })`.
Client tools (the person produces the output): declare them without
`execute` — the UI supplies the output.

## 2. Register how each tool renders

```tsx
import { defineTools } from "@/components/chat/tool-registry"

export const tools = defineTools<ChatMessage>()({
  searchDocs: {
    phase: "searching",            // what the orb shows while it runs
    render: (part) => <Trace><ToolLine part={part} titles={…} /></Trace>,
  },
  askQuestions: {
    client: true,                  // the chat waits for ctx.addOutput
    render: (part, ctx) => …,
  },
  createIssues: {                  // needsApproval on the server
    render: (part, ctx) => …ctx.respond(true)…,
  },
})
```

`render(part, ctx)` gets the fully typed part (`part.input`, `part.output`,
`part.state`) and:

- `ctx.addOutput(output)` — finish a client tool; the turn continues.
- `ctx.respond(approved)` — answer an approval request.
- `ctx.streaming` — the turn is still streaming.

Parts the registry doesn't know fall back to a generic `ToolLine`, so a new
server tool never breaks the transcript — but give every tool a proper entry.

Render `null` for states you don't want to show (e.g. `input-streaming` of a
client tool, so a half-built card never flashes).

## 3. The hook

```tsx
const chat = useAgentChat<ChatMessage>({ transport, tools })
// chat.messages, sendMessage, stop, addToolOutput, addToolApprovalResponse  (from useChat)
// chat.busy      submitted or streaming
// chat.waiting   the last turn waits on the person (open client tool / approval)
// chat.phase     AgentPhase for the orb
// chat.activeIndex  the live assistant turn, or -1
// chat.state     "streaming" | "waiting" | "ready" | "error"
```

It auto-sends after a client tool is answered or approvals are responded to,
and never after a server tool that finished in-stream (that would loop).

## 4. Assemble

```tsx
<ChatThread busy={chat.busy}>
  {chat.messages.map((message, index) => (
    <ChatThreadItem key={message.id} message={message}>
      <ChatTurn
        message={message}
        tools={tools}
        phase={chat.phase}
        active={index === chat.activeIndex}
        streaming={chat.busy && index === chat.messages.length - 1}
        pending={chat.waiting && index === chat.messages.length - 1}
        onToolOutput={(tool, toolCallId, output) => chat.addToolOutput({ tool, toolCallId, output } as never)}
        onApproval={(id, approved) => chat.addToolApprovalResponse({ id, approved })}
      />
    </ChatThreadItem>
  ))}
</ChatThread>

<Composer onSubmit={send}>
  <ComposerInput value={input} onChange={(e) => setInput(e.target.value)}
    placeholder={chat.waiting ? "Answer above to continue…" : "Ask anything…"} />
  <ComposerToolbar>
    <ComposerAttach />
    <ComposerModelSelect models={MODELS} value={model} onValueChange={setModel} />
    <ComposerMic className="ml-auto" />
    <ComposerSubmit busy={chat.busy} onStop={chat.stop} disabled={!input.trim() || chat.waiting} />
  </ComposerToolbar>
</Composer>
```

Empty conversation → `ChatEmpty` with 2–4 `ChatSuggestion`s (icon + a real
task phrased as the person would type it).

### The moments every chat needs (see `example-assistant`, scenarios *metrics* and *deck*)

- **The composer shows what the agent is doing with what you gave it.**
  Capabilities the person switches on are `ComposerToggle`s (Search, Think;
  icon-only on phones). While the agent uses one, `live` lights it in
  `attention`: `live={chat.phase === "searching"}`.
- **Attachments**: files for the next message sit in `ComposerAttachments`
  as removable `AttachmentChip`s; on the sent message they stack above the
  bubble (`UserTurn` renders `file` parts; pass `renderFile` to wrap them in
  `AttachmentPreview`). Reading a file is a trace line ("Read
  q3-board-deck.pdf · 24 pages") followed by what it found (`Findings`).
- **A screen composed for the question**: when no part or widget fits, a
  client tool `renderUI` whose input is A2UI messages renders a `<Surface
  size="sm">`; the person's action is the tool output (scenario
  *compose*). See `surfaces.md`.
- **A whole widget as the answer**: when a widget exists for the data (spend,
  evals, fleet), the tool returns its props and renders it at `size="sm"`
  (`<AiSpend size="sm" {...part.output} />`). Compose a `ChartCard` only
  when no widget fits.
- **A visual answer** is a tool whose output renders a `ChartCard` after its
  trace line, then one or two sentences that say what the chart means.
- **Multi-step work** is a `Plan` streamed as a data part
  (`writer.data({ type: "data-plan", id: "digest", data })`, rendered through
  `defineData` and `ChatTurn data={…}`). Writing the same `id` again updates
  the card; never stream a new card per step.
- **Missing access**: a client tool (e.g. `connectApp`) that renders nothing in
  the transcript; the app docks a `ConnectPrompt` above the composer while
  it waits ("Connect Slack above to continue…" in the placeholder), answers
  the tool on connect, shows the connected line ~2.5 s, removes it. The
  plan's waiting step turns `attention` meanwhile.
- **Errors**: `chat.error` → `<ChatError message onRetry={() =>
  chat.regenerate()} />` as the last thing in the thread, in the person's
  words with what it cost ("Nothing was sent"). If the same route will fail
  again, the retry names another ("Retry with GPT") and switches the model.
  An assistant turn that failed before anything arrived renders nothing.
- **Regenerate** lives in the last turn's actions: `ChatTurn
  onRegenerate={isLast && !busy ? () => chat.regenerate() : undefined}`.
- **Header actions are few and real**: New chat (resets) and Minimise. A
  minimised assistant is a `ChatPill` — orb, the live phase as an eyebrow,
  "Open" turning `attention` when it needs the person — and reopening keeps
  the conversation.

### Layouts

**Full page** — header (orb + title) with a bottom hairline, the thread fills
the middle, content column `mx-auto max-w-[720px]`, composer in a card at the
bottom (`rounded-2xl border bg-card shadow-xs`) inside the same column. Page
background `bg-background`. Nothing under the composer.

**Widget** — `WidgetHeader` (orb + title), **one** `WidgetPanel
className="flex flex-col overflow-hidden p-0"` holding the thread
(`<div className="h-[480px]">`) and the composer below a hairline
(`<div className="border-t border-border/70">`), and an optional
`WidgetFooter` with `ChatStatus`. The conversation and its composer are one
object; don't split them into two panels.

**Embedded parts only** — when the host app already has its chat and you only
add tool UIs, you only need the registry entries (`render`) and the
parts; match the host's container width and keep cards full-width of
the message column.

# Pitfalls

Real bugs met while building uia. Each costs time to rediscover.

**Rings get clipped inside the transcript.** `MessageScrollerItem` uses
`content-visibility`, which clips outside paint. Use `border` (not `ring`) for
card outlines inside messages; keep shadows to `shadow-xs` and give
`PartTransition` its built-in `pb-1`.

**Cards fly in from the top.** `layout` / `layout="position"` on anything in a
streaming transcript animates every reflow while text streams and the scroller
anchors. Appear in place (`initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 4 }}`) and use
`PartTransition` for state changes.

**Hyphens spread out in tables.** `tabular-nums` in Inter also makes "-" and
spaces tabular ("Re - issue"). Apply it to the numeric cell only, never to a
row, list or table.

**Questions come back pre-answered.** Browsers restore form state after a
reload/back. Forms that render agent questions need `autoComplete="off"`
(`AskUser` already does).

**Red fields for a missing answer.** Errors are one quiet line that points at
what's missing ("Pick an option or type your own answer."), no red borders.

**Autostart runs twice (or zero times) in dev.** StrictMode mounts, unmounts,
mounts. Kick off with `setTimeout` inside the effect and clear it in cleanup.

**The chat loops after a server tool.** Don't auto-send just because the last
message has tool results: only after a client tool was answered or approvals
were responded to (`useAgentChat` does this).

**A utility silently disappears.** tailwind-merge drops unknown `text-*`
classes it thinks conflict with `text-sm` etc. That's why the label utility is
`eyebrow`, not `text-eyebrow`. Name custom utilities so they don't look like a
Tailwind group.

**Mono font on the whole page.** The Geist Mono font item targets
`code, kbd, pre, samp`; don't set `font-mono` on `html`/`body`.

**Prose too big inside typeset.** `.typeset` sets its own font size;
`.typeset-chat` resets it to 14px. Use `Markdown`, don't wrap prose in
`.typeset` yourself.

**Dark mode done by hand.** Every token already has a dark value. If you
reach for `dark:` overrides, you're probably using a raw colour. Exceptions
are few and live in the primitives (e.g. disabled ink button).

**Two things spinning.** The orb is the working indicator. A spinner in a
card ("Approval needed" pill) is acceptable only because it signals *waiting
on you*, not *working*. Don't add spinners to tool lines or buttons while the
agent works.

**Typecheck that checks nothing.** The shadcn Vite template's root
`tsconfig.json` has `files: []` and only references the app config, so
`tsc --noEmit` passes no matter what. Use `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`.

**State survives hot reload.** Fast refresh keeps `useState` values, so
changing initial data (positions, mocks) doesn't show until a full reload.
Reload before judging a layout change.

**"Fits" on a narrow desktop window, overflows on the phone.** Desktop
Chrome (and its headless mode) has a minimum window width around 500 px, so
a 390 px screenshot is laid out wider than a phone. Emulate a device, then
list what sticks out past the visual viewport:

```js
const W = visualViewport.width
;[...document.querySelectorAll("body *")]
  .filter((e) => e.getBoundingClientRect().right > W + 1)
  .filter((e) => ![...e.children].some((c) => c.getBoundingClientRect().right > W + 1))
  .map((e) => (e.dataset.slot || e.tagName) + " " + (e.textContent || "").trim().slice(0, 30))
```

An empty list means nothing overflows; then look at it for crushed text.

**iOS zooms in when a field gets focus.** Safari zooms into any input,
textarea or select under 16px. The theme sets every field to 16px on touch
screens (`@media (pointer: coarse)`, `!important` so it beats `text-sm`),
desktop keeps the compact size. Don't fix it with `maximum-scale=1` in the
viewport meta: that also blocks pinch zoom on Android. If a project lacks
the rule, it's missing the uia `theme` item.

**Select items touching the edges.** Padding is on the list, not on groups —
keep uia's `select`; don't wrap items in extra padded divs.

**The orb shrinks to a dim dot in a nav.** `[&_svg]:size-4` on a button
resizes every nested SVG, including the `AgentOrb`, and a still orb is
already at 60% opacity. Size icons in their own wrapper
(`[&>svg]:size-4`) and give the orb `opacity-100` when it stands for a place.

**A row's divider curls at the ends.** `border-t` on a `rounded-*` element
follows the radius. Draw separators as an inset `before:` hairline
(`WidgetListRow` does) and never border one side of a rounded box.

**The first message enters dry.** An empty state that swaps to the thread
on the first send mounts the thread *with* that message, so "present at
mount" would read it as history. `ChatThread` treats a thread that opens
on ≤2 turns as live; don't re-implement turn entrances around it.

**Motion keyframes with `as const` don't type-check** (readonly arrays).
Type the map with `satisfies Record<string, TargetAndTransition>` instead.

**Deep links 404 in production.** Path routes need the host to serve
`index.html` for unknown paths: Cloudflare Workers assets
`"not_found_handling": "single-page-application"` (Vite's dev server
already does it). Keep query flags (`?bare`, `?busy`) when navigating.

**The glow vanishes instead of fading.** Unmounting a card kills its
transition. Switch `tone` to `"default"` first, wait for the drain
(~300 ms), then remove or resolve the card.

**A panel's right edge disappears inside a message.** `WidgetPanel` draws
its hairline with `ring`, which the transcript clips. `Widget size="sm"`
switches it to a real `border`; anything you put in a reply should use
`size="sm"` (or a `border`, never a `ring`).

**shadcn parts fight the eyebrow type.** `cn` can't see inside the
`eyebrow` utility, so a shadcn part's `text-xs font-medium` survives next
to it. Restate `text-[11px]/4 font-normal` when you put eyebrow type on a
shadcn component (StatusBadge does).

**A Sheet's content vanishes while it closes.** A controlled `Sheet` fed by
nullable state renders nothing during its exit animation; keep the last
value until it has closed.

## 1. Anatomy of a widget

```
Widget
├─ WidgetHeader     title · (one scope control on the right)
├─ WidgetPanel      HERO: the number that answers "how is it going?"
│                   + the visual that explains it
├─ WidgetPanel      DETAIL: a titled list / grid that breaks the number down
└─ WidgetFooter     live meta on the left · one action on the right
```

- **Header:** `WidgetTitle` plus, at most, one control that changes the
  *scope* of everything below (environment, region, cluster, month). Put it
  in `WidgetActions` as a `Select` with a leading muted icon. Nothing else:
  no info icon, no settings, no close.
- **Two panels is the default.** A third only when there's a genuinely
  separate block. Never one panel per stat.
- **Footer:** `WidgetMeta` with a `StatusDot tone="success" pulse` when the
  data is live, then cadence and scope ("Live · every 1.6 s · Ashburn"). The
  one action is a `brand` button, `min-w-32`, with three states: idle,
  working (spinner + "-ing" label), done (check + past tense, ~1.8 s) — see
  Deploy policy / Rebalance. Disable it when there's nothing to do.

## 2. The hero: one number and what explains it

```
EYEBROW LABEL                                  secondary stat / sparkline / segmented
1,887,331  unit or / limit   [▲ 4.0%]
META · META · META
──────────────────────────────── (dashed hairline when a row of meters follows)
the visual: MeterBar · TickMeter row · flow graph · scene
```

- One big number per widget (`StatValue`, light, `text-4xl`). Unit or limit
  in `StatUnit` (`/ $1,500`, `/ 52 kW`, `/ 4`). A change goes in a
  `StatusBadge dot={false}` next to it: `success` when up is good, `neutral`
  otherwise — a drop isn't automatically a warning.
- The meta line (`StatMeta`) gives context the number lacks: compared to
  what, and one or two secondary facts. Max three items joined by `·`.
- The right side answers the next question: where it's heading
  ("Projected $2,100"), how it moved (`Sparkline` + "Last 64 s"), or how to
  slice it (`Segmented` with Cost / Balanced / Quality).
- **Then the visual.** Every hero has one, and it shows the reference the
  number is judged against: the budget, the capacity, the limit, the
  baseline. A number against a limit is a `MeterBar` with markers; several
  capacities are a row of three `Stat size="sm"` + `TickMeter`, separated
  from the hero by `border-t border-dashed`.

## 3. Lists are legends

- The detail panel opens with `WidgetSectionTitle` (+ optional eyebrow
  summary under it: "8 nodes · 1 running hot · 1 draining") and continues
  with `WidgetList`: eyebrow column headers, hairline rows.
- Each row is a thing in the visual above. Same colour dot as its segment
  or line; hovering the row lights it up in the visual and dims the other
  rows; clicking selects it when selection drives an action (Invoke
  planner). Hovering the visual does the same back.
- Row anatomy: name (`text-sm`) + its meta as eyebrow (inline and
  `faint` for a provider; under the name and `muted` for specs), then
  numeric columns right-aligned with `tabular-nums`, then state as a
  `StatusBadge`, then a quiet eyebrow column (countdown, count).

## 4. Data visualisation

- **Categorical** (models, routes): `--chart-1…4`, then
  `--muted-foreground` for "other / self-hosted". Don't use `--chart-5`
  for a category; it's orange and reads as attention.
- **Sequential** (heatmaps, intensity): one hue, `--chart-1`, as opacity
  over the card: `color-mix(in oklch, var(--chart-1) N%, transparent)`.
  Never mix the hue with grey (it drifts purple in dark mode). Show the
  scale as a small swatch strip with eyebrow ends ("0% … 100%").
- **Meters:** `TickMeter` for a single ratio (track is the same hue at
  20%); `MeterBar` for a breakdown or when thresholds matter.
- **Lines:** `Sparkline` — no axes, dashed mean, last point marked.
- **Illustrations** (flow graph, isometric scene) are drawn in hairlines
  with `currentColor`/tokens, fill `--card`/`--muted`, and highlight the
  focused thing with `--foreground`, not a new colour. A leader line from
  the focused element to a mono label says its one key fact.
- **Tooltips** for dense visuals: dark (`TooltipContent`), a title row with
  the thing and its kind, then key/value rows (`opacity-60` keys,
  `tabular-nums` values). Open instantly (`delay={0}`).
- States inside a visual: hatched (`repeating-linear-gradient` of
  `--border`) for draining/disabled, near-empty for idle, a small `warning`
  dot for "needs a look". Never a red cell.

## 5. Live and interactive

- Numbers that change use `NumberTicker`; bars and markers animate with
  `springSoft`; transitions between states are opacity/height, never
  slides.
- Simulated data in examples is a small state machine with a clock
  (`setInterval` in an effect, cleaned up). Real data replaces the clock,
  not the components.
- Everything clickable responds: rows, nodes, boxes, segments. If a thing
  looks interactive and isn't, remove the affordance.
- When an action changes the data (Rebalance, Deploy, Invoke), the visual
  shows the consequence (load evens out, version bumps, a box wakes up).

## 6. Copy

- Eyebrows are noun phrases with units: "TOKENS SERVED / S", "COLD START
  P50 170 MS", "ZERO AFTER 12S IDLE".
- Titles are plain nouns: "Fleet health", "Routes", "By model".
- An alert line is `StatusBadge` (the state) + one sentence with new
  information: when, how much, what happens next ("At this pace the budget
  runs out around Oct 23"). Not advice ("Review your budget").
- Button labels are verbs about the thing: "Invoke planner", "Deploy
  policy", "Rebalance".

## 8. Pages

A page is widgets in a column plus, for agent products, the conversation as
a rail. The example is `example-bottega`.

```
┌ header: title · eyebrow summary ─────────── [one scope select] ┐
│ Needs you · N        (decision chips; the only orange)  │ rail: │
│ Section widget (titled list, full width)                │ orb · │
│ Section widget │ Section widget   (2-up at xl)          │ chat  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘
```

- **Header** (`h-14`, sticky, hairline below): page title, an eyebrow
  summary ("5 projetos · 3 no ar"), and one `Select` that scopes the whole
  page. Clicking a row that represents the same thing sets that scope too.
- **What needs the person comes first.** A strip of `DecisionChip`s, each
  opening its full card in the conversation. When empty, one quiet line
  ("Nada esperando você"). Nothing else on the page uses `attention`.
- **Sections are plain `Widget`s** (title outside, panels inside) stacked
  with `gap-8` in a centred column (`max-w-[60rem]`, `px-6 py-8`). Pair
  two at `xl` when they're peers (production · activity).
- **Outcomes over machinery.** For agent products show where each thing is
  (`StageTrack` over the flow), what is live and healthy, and what the agent
  did on its own (a quiet log) — not agents, tasks and tests. Details stay
  one click away.
- **The conversation rail** (`26rem`, `border-l`): header with the
  `AgentOrb`, the agent's name and a status eyebrow ("Esperando você"),
  the thread, the composer at the bottom. Decisions are answered there; the
  page reflects the consequence (stage moves, version changes, log entry,
  the agent confirms in the thread).

## 9. Mobile first

Design at 375 px first, then add columns as space allows. Nothing may
extend past the viewport (a page wider than the phone zooms out and every
tap target shrinks).

- **Lists keep the name and one or two numbers.** Secondary columns get
  `max-sm:hidden` on *both* the header cell and the row cell, and the
  columns are set per breakpoint:
  `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_80px_44px] sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_64px_80px_44px]`.
  Inline metadata that competes with the name (provider eyebrows) hides too.
  A per-row visual that has a numeric twin (Δ next to a comparison bar)
  can go; the number stays.
- **Rows with a wide visual go to two lines:** name · state on top, the
  visual full width below (`col-span-2 order-last`, back to its column at
  `md`). See the projects list in `example-bottega`.
- **Heroes stack:** the secondary stat, sparkline or `Segmented` moves under
  the big number (`flex-col sm:flex-row`); a control that was absolute in a
  corner becomes static (`self-start sm:absolute …`).
- **Meta lines and footers wrap** (`flex-wrap`, `gap-y-*`); badges never wrap
  inside (`StatusBadge` is `whitespace-nowrap`).
- **Side panels: a column at `lg`, a Sheet below.** At `lg` a detail panel
  is an inline third column (non-modal, the list stays usable); below it's a
  full-screen shadcn `Sheet` (focus trap, Esc, scroll lock) with the same
  header and content, rendered once for both (`matchMedia("(min-width:
  64rem)")`). See `example-davinci`.
- **Rails become sheets.** Below `lg` the conversation rail is a full-screen
  sheet opened by a floating `brand` button ("Conversa" + attention count);
  decision chips open the sheet and scroll to their card.
- **Chat on phones:** no avatar beside the agent's messages (the header's
  orb carries presence; the text gets the full width — `AssistantTurn`
  does this); the scroll-to-end button sits bottom-right, off the cards'
  buttons; a full-screen sheet stacks above any floating chrome.
- **Nothing is hover-only.** A phone has no hover and long-press is hidden:
  whatever a mouse reveals on hover, a tap reveals and a second tap lets
  go (`BarSeries` bars, `AttachmentPreview` cards). Check the pointer type
  so a mouse click doesn't undo its own hover:
  `e.nativeEvent.pointerType === "mouse"`.
- **A free-text field gets its own row.** In a form footer (Back · field ·
  Submit) the field takes the full width on phones and the buttons sit
  below it, Back left and Submit right (`flex-wrap`, field
  `max-sm:order-first max-sm:basis-full`; if the input renders inside a
  wrapper, put those classes on the wrapper).
- **Many tabs become a select.** A `Segmented` with more than ~4 options
  turns into a `Select` on phones (`max-md:hidden` / `md:hidden` pair).
- **Check it for real:** emulate a phone (device toolbar or the browser
  tool's mobile preset), not a narrow desktop window — desktop Chrome
  won't go below ~500 px, so headless screenshots at 390 px lie. Then run
  the overflow check from `pitfalls.md`.

## 10. Agent apps: an inbox, not one chat

When an agent works *for* someone (a coordinator, an operator, a reviewer
bot), their attention is the scarce thing. One chat for everything buries
the urgent decision under yesterday's small talk, makes "what's pending?"
a scroll, and loses what was decided. Build the app the example
`example-davinci` shows instead:

```
┌ nav ───────────┬ view (route) ─────────────────────┬ panel ─────┐
│ ◌ davinci      │ 6 decisions need you              │ task / diff│
│ Inbox       6  │ Since 21:00: 7 shipped, 1 stuck,  │ / preview  │
│ THREADS        │ 7 decided for you.                │ (sheet on  │
│ ◌ blog         │ NOW    [card, attention glow]     │  phones)   │
│ ◌ bottega      │ TODAY  [card] [card]              │            │
│ LOOK           │ CAN WAIT [card]                   │            │
│ Projects       │ Answered today · Undo             │            │
│ Decided     7  │                                   │            │
│ Rules       3  │                                   │            │
│ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─  │                                   │            │
│ digest 21:00 ☾ │                                   │            │
└────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┴────────────┘
```

- **Decisions are state, not messages.** The inbox holds only what needs
  the person, grouped by urgency (Now / Today / Can wait). Each card stands
  alone: what, why in one line, the agent's pick marked on its option, and
  the consequence ("If you go with davinci: …"). Mark the exception only
  ("Irreversible"); most things can be undone, so don't badge them.
- **Only the urgent card glows** (`ActionCard tone="attention"`); answering
  drains the glow, then the card sinks out, the cards below glide up, and
  it lands as the newest "Answered today" row (dropping in from above,
  glowing once) with Undo, which sends it back up into its section. When the urgent card scrolls away, a compact "Now" bar pins it.
- **The summary line links**: every count in it ("7 shipped", "1 stuck",
  "7 decided for you") opens the place that explains it.
- **Threads are for talking**, one per project, under the agent's still
  orb. A thread can reference an inbox item; the reference shows the
  item's live status, it doesn't duplicate the card.
- **Look, don't act**: Projects (stage tracks; nothing there needs you, the
  copy says so), "Decided for you" (time, what, why, the rule that did it,
  Undo or Final), Rules.
- **Rules come from agreement.** When the person has gone with the agent's
  pick every time in a category (14 of 14), offer "Make it a rule" on the
  card. Rules list as switches (see SKILL.md, verbs vs switches) with how
  often each applied. Undoing a decision a rule made also offers to drop
  the rule.
- **Nav counts**: only the inbox count uses `attention`; the rest are
  faint. Phones: the nav becomes a `Select` in the header, next to the
  orb (home) and the theme toggle.

# Surfaces: UI the agent composes

When no prebuilt part or widget fits the moment, the agent describes a
screen and uia renders it: a dashboard assembled for this question, a
comparison inside a chat reply, a small form. The format is **A2UI v0.9**
(open spec, https://a2ui.org); the vocabulary is the **uia catalog**.

Three tiers, use the first that fits:

1. **A part or widget** through a typed tool (`tools` registry): the agent
   fills props of something we built (`DecisionCard`, `AiSpend`…).
2. **A surface** (this page): the agent composes from catalog entries.
3. Nothing else: no HTML, no code, no styling from the agent.

## The format, in one example

```json
[
  { "version": "v0.9", "createSurface": { "surfaceId": "reviews", "catalogId": "https://uia.frank-47e.workers.dev/catalog/v1.json" } },
  { "version": "v0.9", "updateDataModel": { "surfaceId": "reviews", "path": "/", "value": { "models": [{ "model": "Sonnet", "pass": 0.847, "cost": 0.09 }] } } },
  { "version": "v0.9", "updateComponents": { "surfaceId": "reviews", "components": [
    { "id": "root", "component": "Section", "title": "Code reviews", "children": ["table", "route"] },
    { "id": "table", "component": "Table", "rows": { "path": "/models" },
      "columns": [{ "key": "model", "label": "Model" }, { "key": "pass", "label": "Pass", "align": "end", "format": "percent" }] },
    { "id": "route", "component": "Button", "label": "Route reviews to Sonnet",
      "action": { "event": { "name": "route_reviews", "context": { "to": "sonnet" } } } }
  ] } }
]
```

- **Flat list with ids**; `children` are ids (or a template
  `{ "path": "/items", "componentId": "row" }` repeated per item, where
  relative paths read the item). Rendering starts at `"root"`.
- **Props are literals or bindings** `{ "path": "/pointer" }` into the data
  model. Data can be updated later (`updateDataModel`) without resending
  components: live dashboards.
- **Actions are named events**, never code. Their `context` resolves
  bindings at click time (form values).
- **Numbers are raw**; `format` (`currency`, `percent`, `integer`,
  `compact`, `duration`, `date`) and the host's `locale`/`currency` turn
  them into text. The agent never formats.
- **No styling from the agent**: only catalog names, enums (`tone`,
  `variant`, `columns`, `gap`, `span`) and data. Taste lives in the
  renderer; every composition looks like uia.

## The catalog (`public/catalog/v1.json`, prompt text in `v1.txt`)

| Group | Entries |
| --- | --- |
| block (prefer when the intent matches) | `DecisionCard`, `Plan`, `Findings`, `AiSpend` |
| layout | `Column`, `Row`, `Grid` (columns 1–4, children `span`, follows its own width), `Section` (title + white panel — the unit of a dashboard), `Card`, `Tabs`, `Divider` |
| data | `Stat` (value, format, unit, delta + `deltaIsGood`, meta), `Meter` (value or segments against max, markers), `Progress`, `BarSeries`, `Sparkline`, `Table`, `List` + `KeyValue`, `StageTrack` |
| display | `Text` (title, body, muted, eyebrow, markdown), `Badge`, `Note` (badge + one sentence of new information), `Empty` |
| input | `Button`, `TextField`, `ChoicePicker`, `CheckBox`, `Slider` (two-way bound through `value`), `Confirm` (required before anything destructive) |

Composition rules the renderer can't enforce, so the agent must:
- One `Section` per question the screen answers; `Grid` of 2 for peers,
  `span: 2` for the wide one (a series, a decision).
- A `Section` leads with its answer: a `Stat` (or a block), then what
  explains it (`Meter`, `BarSeries`, `List`), then at most one `Note`.
- Colour only for state: `tone` on `Badge`/`Note`/`KeyValue`; regressions
  get a tone, improvements stay muted.
- At most one primary `Button` per surface; destructive verbs go through
  `Confirm`.

## Rendering

```tsx
import { Surface } from "@/components/surface/surface"
import { createSurfaceStore, useSurface, surfaceFromMessages } from "@/components/surface/store"
import { uiaCatalog } from "@/components/catalog"

// A page: keep a store, feed it messages as they arrive (stream them).
const store = createSurfaceStore()
store.process(messages)
const surface = useSurface(store, "cost-quality")
<Surface surface={surface} catalog={uiaCatalog} onAction={sendToAgent} onIssue={reportToAgent} />

// Inside a chat reply: a client tool whose input is the messages; the
// person's action is the tool output, and the turn continues with it.
renderUI: {
  client: true,
  render: (part, ctx) => (
    <Surface surface={surfaceFromMessages(part.input?.messages)} catalog={uiaCatalog} size="sm"
      onAction={(a) => ctx.addOutput({ name: a.name, context: a.context })} />
  ),
}
```

- **Streaming**: nothing renders until `root` exists; a child that hasn't
  arrived is a skeleton. Send the data first, then components.
- **Validation**: each node is checked against its schema. An unknown
  component or invalid props drops that node (a placeholder with
  `showIssues`) and calls `onIssue({ componentId, code, message })` —
  send it back so the agent fixes and resends. A node may name a
  `fallback` id. Limits: 400 nodes, depth 16.
- **Size**: `size="sm"` in a chat; layout follows the surface's width
  (container queries), so a `Grid` of 3 is one column in a reply.

## Extending

```tsx
const Deploys = defineComponent({
  name: "Deploys", kind: "block",
  description: "Recent deploys with status; use for 'what shipped'.",
  props: z.object({ items: z.array(z.object({ version: z.string(), status: z.enum(["live", "failed"]) })) }),
  render: (p, ctx) => <MyDeploysWidget items={p.items} size={ctx.size} />,
})
export const catalog = extendCatalog(uiaCatalog, [Deploys], "https://acme.dev/catalog/v1.json")
```

Give the agent `catalogToPrompt(catalog)` (or the published `.txt`) in the
tool description, and publish `catalogToJSONSchema(catalog)` at the
catalog id. Registry: `surface` (runtime), `catalog` + `catalog-*` groups,
bundle `surfaces`; example `example-surface`.
